title: claim-aware-kms-allocator-and-audit-chain-verifier
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: We need stronger enforcement of tenant-scoped key usage and an auditable proof that key operations were permitted by RBAC v2 decisions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: a lightweight kms-allocator service that reconciles tenant claims, region pinning, and key affinity policies to return a canonical key reference for runtime callers; and an audit-chain-verifier that validates signed audit envelopes produced by the allocator and by upstream key-use proxies. The changeset implements policy checks (claim-to-key mapping), a permissive shadow-mode rollout for 3 weeks, and a hard-enforce toggle guarded by feature flags. Design notes: - kms-allocator is a gRPC service (package services/kms-allocator) that accepts a ClaimRequest { tenant_id, key_intent, region_hint, requestor_claims } and returns AllocationResponse { key_ref, policy_applied, signed_audit_envelope }. The allocator consults the policy compiler output (policy/compiled/tenant_affinity.json) and the runtime cache of tenant attributes. - audit-chain-verifier is a pluggable package (pkg/audit/verifier) used by the allocator and by the key-proxy to verify that envelopes are signed by an allowed KMS proxy key and that the chain includes the RBAC decision id for traceability. It also computes a digest that is recorded into the existing immutable-audit log backend. - RBAC v2 mapping: introduced claim-aware mapping additions in policy/compiler/rbac_mapper.go so that attributes from OIDC claims (tenant_zone, residency_policy) influence allowed key pools. This is a conservative extension; when the feature flag rbac_v2_claim_eq is off, behavior is unchanged. - Migration and rollout: added e2e and integration tests, a shadow-mode path that only logs mismatches (no enforcement), migration runner to reconcile existing tenant allocations to the allocator's canonical references, and Clear rollout checklist in docs/security/kms-allocator-rollout.md. Security considerations: - allocator performs least-privileged KMS metadata reads only and never stores plaintext material. - signed audit envelopes use the existing CMK for signing; key usage must be added to the Dedicated KMS allowlist (docs include Anika's request for an operational playbook). - feature flag gating and 2-week shadow analysis required before hard enforcement. Tests and CI: - unit tests for rbac_mapper, allocator request/response validation, and verifier signature checks. - integration tests that exercise tenant region pinning and fallback behavior to soft-enforce older key refs. - added a flaky e2e that failed once in CI (race on local test KMS startup) and was rerun; CI is green after adding a small startup backoff. Backwards compatibility: callers that still send legacy key refs receive a canonical mapping; the allocator returns existing refs for tenants not on the new policy. Rollback plan: flip hard-enforce flag to off and direct traffic to legacy path; migration runner is idempotent. Related: references ENG-2241, SEC-78; impacts Dedicated KMS allowlist (SUP-1423).

files_changed: services/kms-allocator/main.go: added new gRPC server and request validation; key method Allocate(ctx, req) orchestrates policy lookup and envelope signing

services/kms-allocator/allocator.go: core allocation logic (policy consult, cache interaction, canonicalization). Example snippet: func Allocate(ctx context.Context, r ClaimRequest) (AllocationResponse, error) { // validate -> consultPolicy -> signEnvelope -> return }
pkg/audit/verifier/verifier.go: verifier ensures audit envelopes are signed by allowed proxy keys and contains RBAC decision id; adds VerifyEnvelope(envelope) bool
policy/compiler/rbac_mapper.go: extend MAP to include claim filters; small change in MapAttributesFromClaims(claims map[string]string) to include tenant_zone and residency_policy
e2e/tests/kms_allocator_e2e_test.go: tests that simulate tenant with region pin and fallback scenarios
docs/security/kms-allocator-rollout.md: rollout steps, shadow analysis queries, operational playbook
pkg/feature/flags.go: add rbac_v2_claim_eq and kms_allocator_hard_enforce feature gates
integration/fixtures/policies/tenant_affinity.json: sample compiled policy used by tests
e2e/tests/fixtures/test_kms_proxy.sh: local test proxy harness (modified startup backoff to avoid CI race)
review_comments: Diego Morales (2026-02-11): Please expand on the threat model for the allocator. What happens if the allocator is compromised? Response: allocator never exposes plaintext keys and only returns key references; compromise impacts mapping decisions and audit chain but not key material confidentiality. Added section in docs and added tests that assert allocator can't return plaintext.

Anika Patel (2026-02-12): We need operator playbook for adding signing key to Dedicated allowlist and KMS rotation implications. Response: added docs/security/kms-allocator-rollout.md and a short runbook in SUP-1423. Also updated CI to check presence of signing key env var in deploy templates.

Liam O'Connor (2026-02-13): Request to add unit test for malformed envelopes and ensure verifier returns explicit error codes. Response: added VerifyEnvelope negative tests and mapped errors to audit log entries. CI updated accordingly.
Diego Morales (2026-02-15): Minor: prefer backoff config to be configurable via helm values. Response: moved backoff to helm values and updated values.yaml; rebased and pushed fix.
merge_commit_message: squash: introduce claim-aware kms allocator + audit-chain verifier (ENG-2241, SEC-78)
notes: Shadow-mode enabled by default; ops must run 2-week analysis before flipping kms_allocator_hard_enforce. Dedicated customers require KMS allowlist update. CI had one flaky e2e which was addressed by startup backoff and is stable since 2026-02-16.
